(Optional) In OrderReceive, `import api from '@/lib/api'` is used (submit uses api.post), but ProductImport uses raw fetch with localStorage token — inconsistent auth patterns across new components; consider unifying via the api axios instance.
critical_code_review_comments: ProductImport.jsx uses raw fetch+localStorage token instead of the shared axios `api` instance used elsewhere; if auth ever moves to httpOnly-only cookies this will break. Prefer api.post with FormData.
receive endpoint uses float comparison with 1e-9 tolerance — OK for typical qty but note items support fractional units (unit_price>0 check on `it.get('unit_price', 0)`). Confirmed working.
product_import commit path performs sequential awaits inside a for loop — for large sheets (100+ rows) consider bulk_write; not critical for the current use case.
Import preview has no upper-bound row cap; a malicious/large xlsx could DoS. Consider adding max_rows=5000 guard.
Orders.jsx trailing-garbage bug (fixed) was a plain editor slip — indicates E1 should run the frontend build/lint before shipping (would have caught all 3 Orders.jsx bugs immediately).

close_order sets it['received_qty'] = it['quantity'] via local mutation then writes items back — correct, but the DB write for `items` and product stock/movement inserts are not transactional; if the process dies mid-loop stock could be double-counted after retry. Same pattern in receive_order.
